children: With Malaysia moving closer to the next general election cycle in 2027, the window for an interest-rate increase could be narrowing, UOB economists Julia Goh and Loke Siew Ting say in a note. However, Bank Negara Malaysia's confidence in the growth outlook and modestly rising inflation risks leave room for further policy tightening, they say. They have pushed back their forecast for a 25bp hike to 1Q 2027 from their previous expectation of a November increase. UOB expects the policy rate to remain at 3.00% for the rest of 2027. Future rate decisions will depend on growth, inflation and external conditions. While the U.S. midterm results have eased near-term policy uncertainty, renewed protectionist measures, supply-chain disruptions and persistent global inflation could tighten financial conditions and affect Malaysia, UOB adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
